blocks.html: Why is it important
blocks.text: Why is it important

blocks.html: Ensures that polymorphism works safely and predictably.
blocks.text: Ensures that polymorphism works safely and predictably.

blocks.html: Prevents subtle bugs when replacing one implementation with another.
blocks.text: Prevents subtle bugs when replacing one implementation with another.

blocks.html: Allows extensions without breaking existing code.
blocks.text: Allows extensions without breaking existing code.

blocks.html: Maintains consistent interface contracts across hierarchies.
blocks.text: Maintains consistent interface contracts across hierarchies.

blocks.html: Improves reusability and maintainability of abstractions.
blocks.text: Improves reusability and maintainability of abstractions.

blocks.html: How to check if the code follows LSP
blocks.text: How to check if the code follows LSP

blocks.html: Rule 1 — Behavior Preservation
blocks.text: Rule 1 — Behavior Preservation

blocks.html: Subtypes must preserve the behavior promised by the base type.
blocks.text: Subtypes must preserve the behavior promised by the base type.

blocks.html: Check: Replace a base type with each subtype in tests. If behavior changes unexpectedly, LSP is violated.
blocks.text: Check: Replace a base type with each subtype in tests. If behavior changes unexpectedly, LSP is violated.

blocks.html: Rule 2 — No Contract Weakening
blocks.text: Rule 2 — No Contract Weakening

blocks.html: Preconditions in subtypes must not be stricter than in the base type.
blocks.text: Preconditions in subtypes must not be stricter than in the base type.

blocks.html: Check: If a subtype demands extra conditions before methods work, LSP is violated.
blocks.text: Check: If a subtype demands extra conditions before methods work, LSP is violated.

blocks.html: Rule 3 — No Contract Breaking
blocks.text: Rule 3 — No Contract Breaking

blocks.html: Postconditions in subtypes must not be weaker than in the base type.
blocks.text: Postconditions in subtypes must not be weaker than in the base type.

blocks.html: Check: Ensure the method returns values or states that meet or exceed base type guarantees.
blocks.text: Check: Ensure the method returns values or states that meet or exceed base type guarantees.

blocks.html: Rule 4 — Preserve Invariants
blocks.text: Rule 4 — Preserve Invariants

blocks.html: A subtype must not break the conditions (invariants) that the base type guarantees to always hold.
blocks.text: A subtype must not break the conditions (invariants) that the base type guarantees to always hold.

blocks.html: Check: List the base type’s invariants. Verify that every subtype also ensures these invariants remain true in all situations.
blocks.text: Check: List the base type’s invariants. Verify that every subtype also ensures these invariants remain true in all situations.

blocks.html: Invariant (in OOP / LSP context):
blocks.text: Invariant (in OOP / LSP context):

blocks.html: An invariant is a condition or rule that must always hold true for an object of a class, no matter what state it’s in.
blocks.text: An invariant is a condition or rule that must always hold true for an object of a class, no matter what state it’s in.

blocks.html: It’s like a guarantee the class gives about its valid state.
blocks.text: It’s like a guarantee the class gives about its valid state.

blocks.html: Examples:
blocks.text: Examples:

blocks.html: For a Rectangle, width ≥ 0 and height ≥ 0 are invariants.
blocks.text: For a Rectangle, width ≥ 0 and height ≥ 0 are invariants.

blocks.html: For a BankAccount, balance ≥ 0 might be an invariant.
blocks.text: For a BankAccount, balance ≥ 0 might be an invariant.

blocks.html: For a SortedList, the elements are always in ascending order — that’s its invariant.
blocks.text: For a SortedList, the elements are always in ascending order — that’s its invariant.

blocks.html: Rule 5 — Exception Consistency
blocks.text: Rule 5 — Exception Consistency

blocks.html: Subtypes should not throw new unexpected exceptions where the base type wouldn’t.
blocks.text: Subtypes should not throw new unexpected exceptions where the base type wouldn’t.

blocks.html: Check: Review method signatures and runtime behavior for extra error cases.
blocks.text: Check: Review method signatures and runtime behavior for extra error cases.

blocks.html: Rule 6 — Type Replaceability in Client Code
blocks.text: Rule 6 — Type Replaceability in Client Code

blocks.html: Code using the base type should work with any subtype without modification.
blocks.text: Code using the base type should work with any subtype without modification.

blocks.html: Check: Swap base type objects with subtype objects in integration tests. If failures occur, LSP is violated.
blocks.text: Check: Swap base type objects with subtype objects in integration tests. If failures occur, LSP is violated.

blocks.html: Rule 7 — Interface Segmentation for Capabilities
blocks.text: Rule 7 — Interface Segmentation for Capabilities

blocks.html: Avoid forcing subtypes to implement unsupported behavior.
blocks.text: Avoid forcing subtypes to implement unsupported behavior.

blocks.html: Check: If a subtype’s method is empty, throws errors, or is irrelevant, LSP is likely violated.
blocks.text: Check: If a subtype’s method is empty, throws errors, or is irrelevant, LSP is likely violated.

blocks.html: Rule 8 — Test with Real Substitutions
blocks.text: Rule 8 — Test with Real Substitutions

blocks.html: Use real scenarios where subtypes are passed to code expecting the base type.
blocks.text: Use real scenarios where subtypes are passed to code expecting the base type.

blocks.html: Check: Any break in behavior indicates violation.
blocks.text: Check: Any break in behavior indicates violation.
